transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm a graphic designer, and I've been feeling so overwhelmed lately. I can’t stop getting stuck on these awful ‘what if I missed something’ thoughts about my design files, and they’re taking over my workday.
Do you do anything repeatedly, like checking your design files over and over or mentally reviewing them, to try to reduce the anxiety from these thoughts?

Yes, I do that constantly just to cope with the sheer panic of those thoughts. I'll reopen the same file dozens of times, zooming in on every text block, counting how many times I've checked, and re-exporting the artwork over and over. It's incredibly exhausting and eats up my entire evening, but I just can't stop.
Do these repeated thoughts and checking behaviors feel unwanted and hard to control, and do you recognize that they are excessive or unreasonable even though you still feel driven to do them?

Yes, absolutely—they are completely unwanted and so exhausting to deal with. Intellectually, I know that checking a file four or five times is totally unreasonable, but the overwhelming anxiety and that nagging "what if" feeling force me to keep doing it anyway just to get some relief. It really feels like I've lost control over my own mind.
How long have these intrusive thoughts and checking rituals been happening, and do they take up more than an hour a day or significantly interfere with your work or daily life?

They’ve been a major issue for the past year, though it really started building up five years ago when I went freelance. They easily take up several hours a day, often consuming my entire evening. It's completely disrupted my life—I'm missing deadlines, turning down new clients, and I've had to stop gardening and seeing friends altogether.
Do you have any other repetitive behaviors or mental rituals besides checking, such as washing, ordering, counting, or repeating thoughts or phrases to feel safe?

I don't have any rituals like washing or ordering things. However, I do engage in counting, specifically keeping track of exactly how many times I've checked a page. I also obsessively reopen and re-export the files over and over just to make sure they are safe to send.
When you try to resist the checking or stop yourself from doing it, does your anxiety spike until you give in, or do the thoughts feel more like worries you can dismiss?
I absolutely cannot just dismiss them; if I try to resist, my anxiety spikes into pure panic. The only way to quiet that overwhelming feeling is to give in and reopen the files to check them again.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has recurrent, intrusive, unwanted obsessions about having missed errors in design files, accompanied by repetitive checking/counting/re-exporting compulsions performed to reduce severe anxiety. He recognizes the behaviors as excessive, experiences marked distress and loss of control, spends several hours per day on the rituals, and has significant functional impairment with work and social life disruption. This is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
